mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening periods (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the threshold in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5.5% predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to reduced consumer spending and investment demand.
regime_hint: High unemployment and rising wage pressure
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, or UNRATE does not cross the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (industrial production) above 2020 Q4 levels are associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals sustained economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 2020Q4 level for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return during qualifying months (t-test p > 0.05), or HOUST does not exceed the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO below 108 (2017=100 index) combined with a simultaneous rise in GDPC1 above 11200 suggests supply-side weakness, predicting a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 108 AND GDPC1 > 11200 in the same month
regime_hint: Supply shock or contractionary production cycle
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during qualifying events, or proxies move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 197.5 indicates deflationary pressure, which is expected to produce a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via lower discounting.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during deflationary periods, or CPIAUCSL does not fall for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in PAYEMS (employment) by over 10,000 in a month predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market expansion supports corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during such events, or the increase is not above the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (industrial production) for two consecutive months indicate demand softening, forecasting a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < prev AND HOUST < prev for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such dual declines, or proxies move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months in a non-recession regime, it reflects labor market slack and is expected to produce a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via lower discounting of growth prospects.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for three consecutive months and regime is not in recession
regime_hint: Low unemployment and stable macro environment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during qualifying periods, or UNRATE does not fall for three months.
